content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding the PostgreSQL Cost-Based Optimizer and Statistics"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"PostgreSQL relies on a Cost-Based Optimizer (CBO) to determine the most efficient execution plan for any given SQL query. Instead of executing queries blindly, the CBO evaluates multiple execution strategies, estimates the computational cost of each, and selects the one with the lowest total cost."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Role of Statistics"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The accuracy of the CBO depends heavily on database statistics. PostgreSQL collects metadata about the distribution of data within tables and indexes, storing this information in system catalogs like pg_statistic. Without up-to-date statistics, the optimizer might choose a sequential scan over an index scan, severely degrading query performance."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Using the ANALYZE Command"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"The ANALYZE command collects statistics about the contents of tables in the database and stores the results in the pg_statistic catalog. You can run this command manually on a specific table, an entire schema, or the whole database."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"ANALYZE VERBOSE employees;"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"When executed with the VERBOSE option, PostgreSQL outputs progress reports detailing the number of pages and rows sampled during the process."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"How Autovacuum Manages Statistics"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"In modern PostgreSQL deployments, manual execution of ANALYZE is rarely needed for routine maintenance because the autovacuum daemon automatically triggers ANALYZE when a significant number of rows have been inserted, updated, or deleted."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Autovacuum tracks data modification through the pg_stat_user_tables view."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Thresholds for automatic analysis are controlled by parameters like autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor and autovacuum_analyze_threshold."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Inspecting Statistics"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can inspect the collected statistics for a specific column by querying the pg_stats view. This view presents a human-readable interface to the underlying pg_statistic catalog."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"SELECT attname, n_distinct, null_frac FROM pg_stats WHERE tablename = 'employees';"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Tuning Statistics Target"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, PostgreSQL samples a limited number of rows to build statistics. For columns with complex data distributions, you can increase the statistics target for a specific column to improve the accuracy of the CBO."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"ALTER TABLE employees ALTER COLUMN department_id SET STATISTICS 500;\nANALYZE employees;"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Increasing the statistics target causes ANALYZE to collect more detailed frequency histograms, which uses more memory and catalog storage but yields better query plans for highly skewed data."}]
